newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee rebounds to end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee rebounds to end sharply higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures raced higher on Wednesday, retracing early session losses and bouncing back from Tuesday's sharp decline, bolstered by a late fund-led rally, traders said.

CSCE active May coffee jumped 9.05 cents -- or about six percent -- on the day, to end at 166.30 cents, after ranging from 167.00 to 154.00. Spot March ended 7.20 cents higher, at 175.30 cents, while the outer months rose 1.05 to 7.80 cents.

"I think many people felt liquidation of March ahead of first notice day had been completed by mid-morning," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt. "We started to see better trade support at those levels given tight supplies and concerns about available supplies for delivery."
Heavy buying by commodity funds emerged in May and the back months after buy-stops were triggered above 157.50 cents per lb basis the May contract, dealers said.
The market headed lower from the outset -- defying pre-opening expectations -- as speculators liquidated long positions ahead of March first notice day Thursday.
Some dealers said sentiment was dampened by a crop forecast released by Brazil's exporter group Abecafe which pegged the coming 1997/98 harvest at 23.2 million 60-kg bags.

But Dean Witter's Platt said that althoough the forecast was higher than a preliminary Brazilian government projection of between 18 and 20 million bags, the Abecafe estimate was still below the government's forecast of 25 million bags in 1996/97.
"The Brazil estimate is still lower than last year's and it points to a deficit situation," Platt said.
The secretary-general of Abecafe said Wednesday that Brazil is likely to see a production deficit of at least four million 60-kg bags in 1997/98.

"(Total) demand for Brazilian coffee is of the order of 28 million bags and this is a conservative estimate," said Jose Sette at a press conference in Sao Paulo, Brazil. "We will have a deficit of more than four million bags, nearly five million."
Additionally, Platt said monthly inventory data showing a modest increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks was also viewed as friendly.
"It was a confirmation that it is still a tight situation," he said.
The Green Coffee Association of New York reported late Tuesday supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose in January by a modest 15,000 60-kg bags, to 1,264,000 bags.
Traders will be keeping an eye on Colombia, where a powerful earthquake rocked the central-western region of the country on Wednesday.

While there was no immediate news of serious damage or injuries, Colombian national radio reported minor damage, including broken windows in Pereira and Armenia, cities in the heart of the country's central coffee-growing region.
Volume was heavy on Wednesday, at an estimated 21,701 lots, up from Tuesday's official tally of 19,221 lots.
